tiers.label: senior
tiers.note: Representative annual gross N24,000,000 (N2.0M monthly, consistent with the senior medians in the NGA benchmarks: software engineering N1.85M, data N2.15M, product N2.15M, finance N1.54M). Statutory items: employee pension 8 percent of gross = N1,920,000 (Pension Reform Act 2014 applies 8 percent to basic plus housing plus transport; taken here as full gross, so this is the high end of the typical deduction); rent relief N500,000 (Nigeria Tax Act 2025 cap, lower of N500,000 or 20 percent of annual rent). Taxable income = 24,000,000 - 1,920,000 - 500,000 = N21,580,000. PAYE under the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 bands effective 1 January 2026: N330,000 (15 percent of the 2.2M band) + N1,620,000 (18 percent of the 9M band) + N2,011,800 (21 percent of 9.58M above 12M) = N3,961,800. Total statutory deduction = 3,961,800 + 1,920,000 = N5,881,800 = 24.5 percent of gross (24.9 percent if no rent relief is claimed). Excluded: National Housing Fund 2.5 percent of basic, voluntary for private sector employees since the Business Facilitation (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2023; NHIA health premium, no mandatory employee rate (employer borne in practice). Sources: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries Nigeria individual pages (rates page last reviewed 29 May 2026; deductions page covering rent relief and removal of the consolidated relief allowance) and KPMG Flash Alert 2025-168 (bands and 1 January 2026 effective date), both verified 31 August 2026.

tiers.label: lead
tiers.note: Representative annual gross N36,000,000 (N3.0M monthly, sitting between the senior tech medians of N1.85M to N2.15M and the CTO median of N4.0M, and near the finance lead median of N3.08M). Employee pension 8 percent = N2,880,000; rent relief N500,000. Taxable income = N32,620,000. PAYE: N330,000 + N1,620,000 + N2,730,000 (21 percent of the 13M band) + N1,752,600 (23 percent of 7.62M above 25M) = N6,432,600. Total statutory deduction = 6,432,600 + 2,880,000 = N9,312,600 = 25.9 percent of gross (26.2 percent without rent relief). Exclusions as per the senior tier note: NHF (2.5 percent of basic) is voluntary for private sector employees since 2023, and the NHIA levy has no mandatory employee rate. Pension base assumption (basic plus housing plus transport equal to gross) pushes the deduction toward the high end. Bands per Nigeria Tax Act 2025 effective 1 January 2026, verified via PwC and KPMG Flash Alert 2025-168 on 31 August 2026.

tiers.label: executive
tiers.note: Representative annual gross N48,000,000 (N4.0M monthly, matching the CTO median from the TechCabal September 2025 expert survey in the NGA benchmarks; far below large listed bank CEO pay of N195M to N485M a year). Employee pension 8 percent = N3,840,000; rent relief N500,000. Taxable income = N43,660,000. PAYE: N330,000 + N1,620,000 + N2,730,000 + N4,291,800 (23 percent of 18.66M between 25M and 50M) = N8,971,800. Total statutory deduction = 8,971,800 + 3,840,000 = N12,811,800 = 26.7 percent of gross (26.9 percent without rent relief). Above N50M taxable income the marginal rate is 25 percent, so deductions converge toward the high 20s at very high pay. Exclusions and assumptions as per the senior tier note (NHF voluntary in the private sector; NHIA employer borne; pension base taken as full gross). Bands per Nigeria Tax Act 2025 effective 1 January 2026, verified via PwC (page reviewed 29 May 2026) and KPMG Flash Alert 2025-168 on 31 August 2026.

tiers.label: senior
tiers.note: Representative salary 30,000 MAD gross per month (360,000 per year), consistent with senior benchmark medians of 24,000 to 55,000 MAD in the companion mar.json file. Monthly employee deductions: CNSS 4.48 percent of the first 6,000 MAD (ceiling in force through 2026) = 268.80; AMO 2.26 percent uncapped = 678.00; professional expenses abatement 20 percent of gross capped at 2,500 per month (30,000 per year). Net taxable = 30,000 - 268.80 - 678.00 - 2,500 = 26,553.20 per month = 318,638.40 per year. IR per the 2025/2026 annual scale (Loi de Finances 2025, loi 60-24: 0-40,000 at 0 percent, 40,001-60,000 at 10 percent, 60,001-80,000 at 20 percent, 80,001-100,000 at 30 percent, 100,001-180,000 at 34 percent, above 180,000 at 37 percent with 27,400 to deduct): 0.37 x 318,638.40 - 27,400 = 90,496.21 per year = 7,541.35 per month. Total statutory deduction = 268.80 + 678.00 + 7,541.35 = 8,488.15 of 30,000 = 28.3 percent. Scale, abatement and rates verified via Humantal bareme IR 2026 (published 2026-01-12) and EKM Audit 2025 IR guide (2025-04-01); CNSS 4.48 percent with the 6,000 ceiling and AMO 2.26 percent verified via Cleiss (updated 2024) and AJIEL (2026-03-10, ceiling unchanged at 6,000 for 2026; a rise to 8,000 reported by La Vie Eco remains a draft). Single taxpayer, no family deduction, no voluntary CIMR or mutual included.

tiers.label: lead
tiers.note: Representative salary 40,000 MAD gross per month (480,000 per year), consistent with lead benchmark medians of 30,000 to 50,000 MAD in the companion mar.json file. Monthly employee deductions: CNSS 4.48 percent of the first 6,000 = 268.80; AMO 2.26 percent x 40,000 = 904.00; professional expenses abatement capped at 2,500. Net taxable = 40,000 - 268.80 - 904.00 - 2,500 = 36,327.20 per month = 435,926.40 per year. IR: 0.37 x 435,926.40 - 27,400 = 133,892.77 per year = 11,157.73 per month. Total statutory deduction = 268.80 + 904.00 + 11,157.73 = 12,330.53 of 40,000 = 30.8 percent. Legal basis and verification identical to the senior tier: 2025/2026 IR scale from Loi de Finances 2025 (loi 60-24) via Humantal (2026-01-12) and EKM Audit (2025-04-01); CNSS 4.48 percent capped at 6,000 MAD and AMO 2.26 percent uncapped via Cleiss (2024) and AJIEL (2026-03-10). Single taxpayer, no family deduction, no voluntary CIMR included.

tiers.label: executive

Monthly employee deductions: CNSS 4.48 percent of the first 6,000 = 268.80; AMO 2.26 percent x 65,000 = 1,469.00; professional expenses abatement capped at 2,500. Net taxable = 65,000 - 268.80 - 1,469.00 - 2,500 = 60,762.20 per month = 729,146.40 per year. IR: 0.37 x 729,146.40 - 27,400 = 242,384.17 per year = 20,198.68 per month. Total statutory deduction = 268.80 + 1,469.00 + 20,198.68 = 21,936.48 of 65,000 = 33.7 percent. Legal basis and verification identical to the other tiers: IR scale from Loi de Finances 2025 (loi 60-24, top rate 37 percent, exemption threshold 40,000) via Humantal (2026-01-12) and EKM Audit (2025-04-01); CNSS 4.48 percent capped at 6,000 MAD and AMO 2.26 percent uncapped via Cleiss (2024) and AJIEL (2026-03-10). Fixed salary only; executive variable pay is excluded, and variable is taxed at the same statutory rates when paid. Single taxpayer, no family deduction, no voluntary CIMR included.

tiers.label: senior
tiers.note: Representative senior salary 3,000 USD per month, 39,000 USD per year gross including the 13th month salary (decimo tercer mes). Employee social security: CSS 9.75% plus Seguro Educativo 1.25% = 11.00% of gross = 4,290 USD; the 9.75% employee rate is unchanged by Ley 462 de 2025, which raised only the employer rate (PwC tax summary reviewed August 2026; Morgan and Morgan alert April 2025; Deel CSS guide 2026). ISR base = 39,000 minus 4,290 deductible CSS = 34,710; DGI scale (verified 31 August 2026: 0% to 11,000, 15% on 11,000-50,000, 25% above 50,000) gives ISR = 15% x 23,710 = 3,556.50 USD. Total 7,846.50 USD = 20.1% of gross. No itemized deductions or education credits applied; if the reduced 7.25% employee CSS rate applies to the 13th month (as reported by Panama America payroll coverage), the total falls by about 0.2 points.

tiers.label: lead
tiers.note: Representative lead salary 7,000 USD per month, 91,000 USD per year gross including the 13th month salary, consistent with Michael Page gerencia-level medians (6,000-8,000 for finance and IT management). Employee CSS 9.75% + Seguro Educativo 1.25% = 11.00% x 91,000 = 10,010 USD. ISR base = 91,000 minus 10,010 = 80,990; DGI scale gives 5,850 + 25% x (80,990 minus 50,000) = 13,597.50 USD. Total 23,607.50 USD = 25.9% of gross. No itemized deductions or education credits applied; employee CSS rate unchanged in 2026 (Ley 462 de 2025 raised employer side only).

Total 47,381.25 USD = 29.2% of gross. No itemized deductions or education credits applied; employee CSS rate unchanged in 2026 (Ley 462 de 2025 raised employer side only).

tiers.label: senior
tiers.note: Representative senior gross of 3,000 USD per month (36,000 USD per year, consistent with the senior medians benchmarked for Lebanon), converted at the fixed 89,500 LBP per USD. Income tax per the 2024 Budget Law scale (2/4/7/11/15/20/25 percent on annual brackets of 360M/900M/1.8B/3.6B/7.2B/13.5B LBP, in force since 1 January 2024): taxable income of 2,728.8M LBP after the 450M LBP single-taxpayer deduction and deductible NSSF gives tax of 193.97M LBP (about 2,168 USD, 6.0 percent). Employee NSSF is 3 percent for sickness and maternity on a base capped at 120M LBP per month (ceiling effective July-August 2025 per NSSF Memo 805), i.e. 43.2M LBP (483 USD, 1.3 percent), for a total of about 7.4 percent of gross. End-of-service indemnity is employer-paid and excluded.

tiers.label: lead
tiers.note: Representative lead gross of 4,500 USD per month (54,000 USD per year, about 4,833M LBP at 89,500 LBP per USD). Income tax: taxable income of 4,339.8M LBP after the 450M single-taxpayer deduction and deductible NSSF gives 91.8M (through 1.8B LBP) plus 198M at 11 percent plus 110.97M at 15 percent, totaling 400.77M LBP (about 4,478 USD, 8.3 percent). Employee NSSF adds the capped 43.2M LBP (483 USD, 0.9 percent), for a total of about 9.2 percent of gross. A non-working spouse and children would raise deductions (plus 225M LBP spouse and 45M LBP per child) and lower this by roughly one to two points. End-of-service indemnity is employer-paid and excluded.

tiers.label: executive
tiers.note: Representative executive gross of 7,500 USD per month (90,000 USD per year, about 8,055M LBP at 89,500 LBP per USD). Income tax: taxable income of 7,561.8M LBP after the 450M single-taxpayer deduction and deductible NSSF gives 289.8M (through 3.6B LBP) plus 540M at 15 percent plus 72.36M at 20 percent, totaling 902.16M LBP (about 10,079 USD, 11.2 percent). Employee NSSF adds the capped 43.2M LBP (483 USD, 0.5 percent), for a total of about 11.7 percent of gross. Because the NSSF base is capped so low, the deduction share is driven almost entirely by the progressive scale, which tops out at 25 percent above 13.5B LBP (about 150,800 USD per year). End-of-service indemnity is employer-paid and excluded.

tiers.label: senior
tiers.note: Representative senior gross of MXN 55,000 per month (660,000 per year, consistent with the 50,000-62,500 medians found for senior developers and data engineers). ISR: 2026 monthly tariff (Anexo 8 RMF 2026, in force since January 2026, brackets raised 13.21 percent for accumulated inflation) applied to the taxable base of 53,628.80 (gross minus worker IMSS) gives 5,665.16 fixed plus 23.52 percent of 18,265.97 = 9,960.91. Worker IMSS = 1,371.20 (2.0 percent of SBC for invalidez y vida 0.625, cesantia y vejez 1.125 and prestaciones en dinero 0.25, plus 0.40 percent on the SBC above 3 minimum wages of 9,577.22 per month at 315.04 daily per CONASAMI, plus 0.375 percent above 3 UMA of 3,566.22 per month, UMA 117.31 daily per INEGI from 1 Feb 2026); subsidio al empleo is 0 above 7,382.33. Total 11,332.11 per month, 20.6 percent of gross, assuming SBC equals gross salary and excluding employer charges.

tiers.label: lead
tiers.note: Representative lead gross of MXN 105,000 per month (1,260,000 per year, matching the Gerente de Contabilidad average of 105,000 and the 92,500-150,630 lead range found). ISR 2026 monthly tariff on the taxable base of 102,680.98 gives 10,457.09 fixed plus 30.00 percent of 46,944.30 = 24,540.38. Worker IMSS is capped because the SBC ceiling is 25 UMA (2,932.75 daily, about 89,155.60 per month), so the same rate components as the senior tier yield a maximum of 2,319.02, only 2.21 percent of gross; subsidio al empleo is 0. Total 26,859.40 per month, 25.6 percent of gross.

tiers.label: executive
tiers.note: Representative executive gross of MXN 183,750 per month (2,205,000 per year, matching the Director de Tecnologia and Director de RRHH averages, with Director de Finanzas at 191,250 and the Buk CEO median at 233,000). ISR 2026 monthly tariff on the taxable base of 181,430.98 gives 37,009.69 fixed plus 34.00 percent of 39,550.32 = 50,456.80. Worker IMSS stays capped at the 25 UMA ceiling (89,155.60 per month) at 2,319.02, which falls to 1.26 percent of gross, so the social security share declines at this level while total statutory deductions reach 52,775.82 per month, 28.7 percent of gross.
